new_statements.translation: 2.1.5.1. Stress. In Barí intensity stress is of little relevance. Given its characteristics, from the functional point of view this stress is a unit that is not distinctive and rather contributes to the demarcation of the word in the syntagmatic chain. [...] Its position in the word is predictable; it is assigned independently of the melodic pitch of the syllable it falls on, of the number of syllables of the word, of the class the word belongs to, or of any other factor, and it is always found on the last syllable of the word. Only when the word carries a suffixed morpheme {-na} does the stress, which keeps its original position, end up on the penultimate syllable.
new_statements.citation: Mogollón Pérez, María Cristina. 2000. Fonología de la lengua barí. In María Stella González de Pérez & María Luisa Rodríguez de Montes (eds.), Lenguas indígenas de Colombia: una visión descriptiva, 719-727. Santafé de Bogotá: Instituto Caro y Cuervo.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Non-contrastive intensity (word-level) stress on the final syllable of the word, regardless of tone, length or word class; when the suffix -na is added the stress stays on the stem-final syllable, so it surfaces on the penult (daˈku 'pot' ~ daˈkuna; bitnukˈbĩ 'point' ~ bitnukˈbĩnã; kitˈtu 'foot' ~ kittubitnukˈbĩ 'toe'; nunaˈba 'dog'; ˈku 'louse'). The language is additionally tonal: two lexically contrastive pitch levels (low vs. non-low/high), with a possible grammatical function, and stress is explicitly independent of pitch. Quesada 2004's Venezuelan transcriptions ([ba.ˈri.dʒi] bari-PL, [la.bah.ˈdo]) are consistent with stem-final stress but he makes no statement.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Yes: 'Va acompañando en una misma palabra, de otros acentos considerados secundarios y de variaciones en la altura de las sílabas. Estos otros acentos se encuentran en palabras compuestas y equivalen, en verdad, a los acentos de las palabras aisladas.' — secondary stresses occur only in compounds and are the (final) stresses of the component words.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the suffix {-na}: stress keeps its stem-final position, yielding penultimate stress on the suffixed word. Author adds that the stress is too weak to condition segmental changes and that it is therefore left unmarked in transcriptions (p. 723; p. 725 fn. 1: 'Dadas las características y la funcionalidad del acento en barí, no se ha considerado rasgo relevante en la siguiente transcripción').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('acento de palabra'), citation forms and compounds; data collected 1987-88 at Birikaira (Serranía de los Motilones, Norte de Santander, Colombia), i.e. Colombian Barí. Tone described as lexical (two levels) with tone sequences in disyllables/trisyllables and 'subordinación tonal' in NPs; the author states tone research was only beginning.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement describes Colombian Barí as spoken at Birikaira (Serranía de los Motilones, Norte de Santander), fieldwork 1987-88; Glottolog bari1297 lists no dialect subdivisions, so no dialect-level glottocode. Quesada 2004 (Venezuelan Barí, Maracaibo/Boksí speakers) is the other variety; its transcriptions show stem-final stress under suffixation but no rule statement. Glottolog's 'Yokwe, Bari phonology' is probably the Nilotic Bari [bfa] (name collision), unverified.
